common_name: Kin Kan Leopard Plant (Gold-Edged Spring Farfugium)

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants out in spring once frost danger passes, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring into consistently moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, where the clump can spread wider than it is tall over time. The large, rounded, glossy leaves emerge in spring edged in a narrow band of creamy yellow, an effect that typically softens and fades to solid green as summer heat sets in. Clusters of yellow daisy-like flowers appear on tall stalks in autumn above the foliage mound. Keep soil from drying out, since the broad leaves wilt readily in dry spells, and mulch the crown over winter at the colder end of its range.

common_name: Ferris Wheel Leopard Plant (Thick-Leaved Jagged-Edge Farfugium)

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants out in spring into reliably moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full shade.

directions: Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, including rain garden margins and other spots that stay damp. This compact leopard plant selection is a thought to be a tetraploid, with leaves noticeably thicker and heavier-textured than the species, and edges that develop a distinctive jagged, scalloped look most pronounced in late summer and fall. Tall scapes of golden-yellow, daisy-like flowers rise well above the foliage clump in October and November. Its dense, low habit suits shaded border fronts and container plantings where the bold, textured leaves can be viewed closely.

common_name: Lunar Landing Leopard Plant (Crinkled Crater-Leaf Farfugium)

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants out in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part sun to full shade.

directions: A selection arising from the rounded-leaf 'Ryuto' type, grown in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in part sun to full shade. Its dark green leaves are so heavily crinkled and cratered that the formerly rounded blade becomes deeply puckered and almost unrecognizable as a leopard plant leaf, an effect that intensifies as the clump matures. It forms a tidy, low mound well suited to a shaded rock garden niche or collector's container display, and like other Farfugium it sends up yellow daisy-like flowers in fall. Protect from hard freezes and keep soil consistently moist, since the textured leaves wilt quickly if allowed to dry out.
